body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: c7c5b1ef747adab717b97d60026cb22e37f9c25e -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. The review is at the safety-floor level (collisions, rapids in stock).

### What looks good
- No product code changes. The diff is only `crates/app/tests/flute_reach.rs` and `docs/decisions/3811-flute-reach-rapid-reading.md`.
- The test now pins the cause, not a count that follows the ring plan.
- The 25 mm flute twin (a debug test, in the quick gate) asserts no `ShankHit`, `RapidInPart`, `RapidInStock` or `Gouge`. Thus every contact of the 10 mm case comes from the short flute.
- The decision file obeys the format: what, why, what was dropped, cost.

### The post blocks every finding (proof from the code)
- `Warning::blocks_post` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:443-450`) is true for every kind except `Scallop`, `ProbeSearch`, `SinkerFinishOrder`, `DrillUndersize`, `StrategyFallback` and `FluteShort`. Thus `RapidInPart`, `RapidInStock`, `ShankHit` and `Gouge` all block.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs:1319-1324` writes each blocking warning of the cache as a WARN record.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs:721-727` refuses the post when the engine returns a warning (`post blocked - N warning(s)`).
- `named_first` asserts that `post_setup_unwritten` refuses (`flute_reach.rs:171-172`). The run below confirms it.
- The P1 issues #3824 and #3825 describe the same lifts at (46.482, 123.140) and (-46.500, 123.542). #3825 says that the re-entry is a named plunge at the plunge feed, not a rapid. No case passes silently. I agree that #3811 is not a P1.

### Results merged with main (locally, Windows)
Trial merge of `c7c5b1ef7` with `origin/main` `80f1dc364`: clean, no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test flute_reach -- --include-ignored` | 4 passed, 0 failed (27.5 s) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test flute_reach -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Local mutation check (not committed)
I injected one warning into the heavy test after `named_first(10.0)`, then ran the test in release:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| `RapidInPart` on a horizontal rapid (move 253, (46.49, 123.26) to (-46.50, 123.54) at Z 32) | FAILED at line 128: `rapid 253 is a lift or a drop, not a traverse through the part` |
| `RapidInStock` | FAILED at the last assert |
| `Gouge` | FAILED at the last assert |

Thus a side rapid through the part, a rapid through stock, or a gouge makes the test red.

### Heavy lanes
- AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556): a P2 PR gets no heavy step.
- On request, this review ran the `flute_reach` heavy test in release (above): green.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. A vertical rapid drop of the cutter itself into the part passes the heavy test alone, because it is vertical and its low end is under the part top. The 25 mm twin catches that case, because the cutter meets the part with any flute. Keep the two tests together if one of them moves.
2. Upper bound: I recommend `rapids.len() <= 9` as an added assert. A later fix of #3824/#3825 lowers the count and does not break the bound. A new ring plan that adds more lifts at these points then shows as a red test, not as silent growth. This is optional, because each such lift still blocks the post.
3. The readings are from Windows only. Issue #3811 asks for a green result in release on macOS and Linux. The new asserts do not depend on a count, so a platform difference is less probable. The cut gate on Linux is the first check on another OS.
4. The real fix of these lifts stays with #3824 and #3825. A reading change is correct now, because the findings are real and the post holds.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
